messages:
Mira Cheng: Heads-up — canary for rwd-lite-int4 shows a parse_success_rate drop from 99.6% -> 93.2% once batching>1 is enabled. noticed this on the 'funcall' eval.
Devon Park: whoa that's sizable. Is it only on int4 or seen on float16 too?
Mira Cheng: float16 baseline stable ~99.7% with same workloads. int4 regressed only when batch_size >= 2. single-request paths look fine.
Samir Patel: any correlation with prompt/system message length or certain schema types?
Mira Cheng: yes — structured outputs with long system preambles and nested JSON templates. Seems like token-splitting at batch boundaries.
Alen Gomez: can you paste the eval command and a short example of failing output?
Mira Cheng: sure:
```
./tools/evals/funcall_check.py --model rwd-lite-int4 --canary 2000 --batch 4 --schema samples/schemas/checkout.json --prefix-file experiments/long_system.txt
```
Failing sample (truncated):
```
Assistant: {"order": {"items": ["widget", "gadget"], "total": 49.99}, "payment": {"method": "credit_card"

...then next chunk in batch starts with "number":"4242..." -> JSON broken across responses
```
Lisa Huang: looks like the model is outputting a contiguous JSON that gets split across streaming boundaries. downstream parser gets partial JSON and we count it as parse failure.
Devon Park: is this a model decoding artifact (e.g. early EOS insertion) or just a transmission/batching boundary? Could be tokenization changes after quantization.
Samir Patel: hypothesis: int4 quantization changed tokenization logits near punctuation, causing the model to prefer splitting sequences across examples when we interleave KV caches for batching.
Mira Cheng: telemetry shows majority of failures are suffix-truncation rather than corruption — the chunk ends mid-string. parse errors: unexpected end of input.
Alen Gomez: quick mitigation ideas: 1) disable batching for structured-output route in canary; 2) insert explicit sentinel token between responses; 3) force per-example flushing of KV cache boundaries; 4) post-parse repair heuristics.
Lisa Huang: sentinel tokens are low-effort — canary to try special token like <JSON_END> appended by system and removed after parse. But must check it doesn't affect generation.
Devon Park: also try adjusting batch scheduling to avoid interleaving responses for different requests at kernel level. Maybe we can enforce contiguous generation per request for structured routes.
Samir Patel: let's reproduce locally with smaller harness. I'll run a focused AB test comparing batch=1 vs batch=4 with same seeds and show token-level diffs.
Mira Cheng: run plan I executed in sandbox:
```
# spawn 500 paired requests
python experiments/repro_batch_split.py --model rwd-lite-int4 --pairs 500 --batch 4 --prefix experiments/long_system.txt --seed 42 --save token_traces.jsonl
```
Results: parse_success_rate(batch=1)=99.5%, batch=4=93.1%, median funcall_latency +18ms, token_span_split events correlate with parse failures.
Devon Park: ok can we get token_traces for a couple failing pairs to inspect alignment? also attach model logits around punctuation.
Mira Cheng: uploaded short traces to s3://redwood-canary/rwd-lite-int4/3109991234/traces.zip
Alen Gomez: if it's quant-specific, run the same harness on the float16 variant and a different int4 quant profile (per-channel vs per-tensor) — helps pinpoint quantization mode bug.
Samir Patel: agreed. I'll queue int4-perchannel canary and float16 baseline overnight. also will try decreasing max_tokens_per_batch to 64.
Lisa Huang: we should also instrument the runtime to tag batch boundaries in streaming frames so parser can choose to wait for follow-up frame before failing (soft-retry). even a 50ms wait could turn many failures into success.
Devon Park: note: can't add arbitrary latency for all customers. limit to structured-output routes behind a flag and use heuristic: if frame ends in non-whitespace or inside quotes, and last char not one of [}\]], then wait 20ms.
Mira Cheng: agreed. I'll prototype a parser-wait heuristic in the client shim and run it against the 2k canary set.
onboard-bot: Canary job queued: rwd-lite-int4-batch-split-investigation-3109991234 -> job_id: canary-310999-1
ci-bot: Test run started: int4-perchannel vs int4-pertensor vs float16 (overnight). logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/canaries/3109991234
Samir Patel: one more thought — KV cache reuse between batched requests may produce context mixing if cache indexing isn't fully resetting per instance when using shared buffers. I'll audit the runtime index offsets tomorrow.
Alen Gomez: action items: Samir (runtime audit + per-channel int4 canary), Mira (parser shim prototype + sentinel canary), Devon (scheduling tweak PR draft), Lisa (measure latency impact of parser-wait heuristic). We'll reconvene in ~24h.
Mira Cheng: thanks — I'll update thread with the first quick sentinel canary results once ready. :thumbsup:
Devon Park: thanks all, logging this into the onboard runbook under "structured-output/int4-batch-split."
